clue.text: Upset — the result of being caught out?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to topple something over

definitions.text: the result of being caught out?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: a batter's knock (innings) is over once they are caught

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a knock is an innings, so being caught out leaves the knock over; the question mark flags that playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset a vase is to topple it, the same action as the phrasal verb in the grid.

clue.text: Problem with delivery of brief message to say dance called off

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an illegal ball bowled in cricket

definitions.text: brief message to say dance called off
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: a two-word notice that there will be ..., i.e. no dance

explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' sounds like the post, but in cricket a delivery is a ball bowled; a ball is also a formal dance.
explanation.definitionFit: An illegal bowl in cricket, for overstepping the crease, is a fault in the bowler's delivery.

clue.text: Administrative area runs out of land

indicators.note: out of says the runs letter is taken away from the word for land

parts.note: a land is a country
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone describes a region whose players score runs out of the land, or a district fleeing the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain and Ireland a shire is a unit of local government, the larger regional division.

clue.text: Free cycling store

indicators.note: cycling says the letters of the phrase rotate, the back half coming round to the front

parts.note: to free is to let out

explanation.surface: An offer of a free cycle storage space, or a bike shop giving things away.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotating LET OUT moves OUT to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A retail shop is often called an outlet, as in a factory outlet selling goods.

clue.text: Older nobleman that is king

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A description of an aged aristocrat who also happens to be monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from before is prior in time; 'older' and the answer both mean dating from a previous time.

clue.text: Rolling spliff, rising politician enters in casual footwear

indicators.note: enters says the reversed politician goes inside the reworked letters
rolling a joint suggests mixing up these letters

parts.note: anagram fodder; a spliff is a cannabis cigarette

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: POL is short for politician

explanation.surface: A laid-back scene of someone rolling a joint while a politician walks in wearing beach sandals.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' turns the politician upward, and that reversed piece slots into the rolled letters just before their final S.
explanation.definitionFit: These rubber sandals held on by a thong between the toes are informal summer shoes.

clue.text: Pan-Syrian manoeuvres tell a story

indicators.note: manoeuvres suggests the letters being moved about into new positions

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A report of military exercises across all of Syria.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to recount a long, often embellished tale, borrowed from sailors twisting rope fibres.

clue.text: The economy of second cut over point?

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first pieces sit above the next one

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim
a ness is a headland or point of land

explanation.surface: A cricket question: whether trimming a second over affects a bowler's economy rate at point.
explanation.definitionFit: Economy in the sense of frugality, using little, matches leanness or scantiness.

clue.text: Backsliding students make an error

indicators.note: backsliding says the word slides backwards, read in reverse

parts.note: pupils are students

explanation.surface: Students who fall back into bad habits get things wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To blunder or make a mistake is the phrasal verb meaning to slip.

clue.text: Military order concerning spin

parts.note: about means concerning
a spin is a turn

explanation.surface: A parade-ground command about spinning round.
explanation.definitionFit: The drill command tells soldiers to face the opposite direction, a standard parade instruction.

clue.text: Old member of the Lords welcoming new No.1 at Lord's?

indicators.note: welcoming says the peer takes the new letter inside

parts.note: a peer sits in the House of Lords

explanation.surface: An ageing peer greets a fresh arrival at the London cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground; the first batter in is the number one.
explanation.definitionFit: The batter who goes in first at the top of the order is the opening batsman, number one.

clue.text: Solid tent flaps fitted well

indicators.note: flaps suggests the letters flapping about loose into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Camping talk: a sturdy tent whose flaps are well made.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that slipped neatly into place or blended with a group is said to have sat snugly.

clue.text: Quiet challenge to Macduff: continue sporting behaviour

parts.note: P is piano, quietly in music
Macbeth's defiant 'Lay on, Macduff' in Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean duel framed as a plea for fair play.
explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth challenges Macduff with 'Lay on, Macduff' in their final fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee calls for the game to keep going rather than stop, so sport carries on.

clue.text: After swapping tips, use pronged tool for task on the farm

indicators.note: swapping tips says the two words exchange their opening letters

parts.note: to wield a tool is to use it
a fork has prongs

explanation.surface: Advice on handling a pitchfork for a farm chore.
explanation.walkthrough: Exchanging the first letters of WIELD and FORK gives FIELD WORK.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour carried out in the open meadows rather than in a barn is agricultural toil.

clue.text: Compelling points in favour of Conservative elected head of government

parts.note: E and N are compass points
for means in favour of
in means elected, as a party voted in

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the next word

parts.note: supplies its first letter

explanation.surface: Arguments for a Conservative being voted in to lead the government.
explanation.definitionFit: Compelling someone, making them obey, is imposing a rule upon them by force.

clue.text: Nature is adapting, beginning to make medicinal fluid

indicators.note: adapting says the letters change form into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the next word

parts.note: supplies its first letter

explanation.surface: Nature evolving to produce a healing liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood serum containing antibodies is given as a remedy against specific infections or toxins.

clue.text: Discover charred remains in this?

indicators.note: read as dis-cover: strip the covers, the outside letters, off the word for charred

parts.note: burnt means charred

explanation.surface: Where would you find the ashes left after a cremation?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discover' is split as dis-cover, uncovering BURNT by removing both outside letters; the whole clue also describes a vessel for ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cremated ashes are kept in a vase-like container, so the remains are found inside one.

clue.text: Exploit Aussies regularly

indicators.note: regularly says take letters at even intervals, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: fodder from which every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A complaint that Australians are routinely taken advantage of.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit a resource is to put it to work or take advantage of it.

clue.text: Lop top off slight protuberance

indicators.note: lop the top off says remove the first letter, the top in a down clue

parts.note: a snub is a slight or insult

explanation.surface: Gardening advice to trim a small lump off a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A small knob or lump projecting from a surface is a bump, the core sense of the short word.

clue.text: Money from bookie wife lost which could be declared

indicators.note: lost says the wife letter goes missing from the word

parts.note: winnings are what a bookmaker pays out

explanation.surface: A gambler's wife lost the money collected from a bookmaker, money that perhaps should be declared for tax.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket captain can declare an innings closed; declaring winnings to the taxman is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a captain may close a team's batting spell early by declaring it.

clue.text: Men in white coats fill upper-class parliamentarians with rage

parts.note: U denotes upper-class

indicators.note: fill says the rage goes inside the parliamentarians

parts.note: MPs are members of parliament
ire is rage

explanation.surface: Posh politicians being driven mad, with men in white coats coming to take them away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men in white coats' suggests asylum attendants; cricket officials wear white coats.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket officials traditionally wear long white jackets on the field while adjudicating the match.

clue.text: Decline romantic poet initially?

indicators.note: initially says take the first letter of each of the poet's names, the way she signed her work

parts.note: Elizabeth Barrett Browning, Victorian poet of the love poems Sonnets from the Portuguese

explanation.surface: A query about whether a love poet's reputation is fading.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide going out is a falling away, so the word also means to wane or diminish.

clue.text: He'll drive Sierra garaged by superhero

indicators.note: garaged by says the Sierra is kept inside the superhero, as a car in a garage

parts.note: Batman is a superhero
S is Sierra in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A superhero parks a Ford Sierra car in his garage before going for a drive.
explanation.walkthrough: A drive is a cricket shot, so the one who drives is the batter, not a motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: A batter strikes the ball with an attacking shot called a drive.

clue.text: Ladies' family getting brief visit?

parts.note: the ladies is a toilet, a loo
kin is family

explanation.surface: A quick trip to the ladies' room with relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: A loo is a toilet; 'the Ladies' is the women's toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A short call on someone is a quick glance in, also a chance to take part.

clue.text: Tree which has a sweet spot in the middle?

definitions.text: Tree which has a sweet spot in the middle?

parts.words: Tree which has a sweet spot in the middle?
parts.note: cricket bats are made from the wood of this tree, and a bat's sweet spot is the best place on the blade to hit the ball

explanation.walkthrough: A sweet spot sounds like fruit or sap, but it is the ideal striking area of a cricket bat, which is made of this tree's timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket bats are carved from this tree's timber, and the word stands for the bat itself.

clue.text: Extra feature of novel, e.g. by Eliot

indicators.note: feature of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A characteristic of a George Eliot novel, such as Middlemarch.
explanation.walkthrough: An extra in cricket is a run not credited to the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket this run, scored after the ball glances off the batter's body, counts as a sundry not off the bat.

clue.text: Rotter ordered out of date goods

parts.note: bade is an old-fashioned past tense of bid, meaning ordered
G is short for good, so two goods are GG

explanation.surface: Someone ordered stale stock and ended up with spoiled produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of date' suggests food past its date, but it marks the old-fashioned verb form.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotter is a cad or scoundrel, a person of bad character.

clue.text: It compensates one for being out

definitions.text: It compensates one for being out

parts.words: It compensates one for being out
parts.note: being out here means on strike from work, and unions pay members money while they are out

explanation.walkthrough: Among the cricket clues 'out' suggests a dismissal, but here it means away from work in an industrial dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: Unions give members money to replace lost wages while they take industrial action.

clue.text: Copyright interior from Ikea seen in comic strip

indicators.note: seen in says these letters appear inside the word for comic

parts.note: a wit is a comic, a funny person

indicators.note: interior from picks the middle letters of the next word

parts.note: supplies its middle letters

explanation.surface: Copyrighted Ikea furniture turning up in a cartoon strip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic strip' reads as one thing, but 'strip' is the definition: the pitch in cricket is a strip.
explanation.definitionFit: The rolled turf between the stumps in cricket is called the pitch, also known by this name.

clue.text: Half a trifle?

parts.note: the phrase means something trivial, and a half of weak beer is a small measure of drink

explanation.walkthrough: A trifle suggests the pudding, but here it means something unimportant; a half-pint is the small beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for something trivial or unimportant originally meant weak ale.

clue.text: Dismissed peacekeeping force captured in heavy defeat

indicators.note: captured in says the force is held inside the defeat

parts.note: a rout is a heavy defeat
UN, the United Nations, sends peacekeepers

explanation.surface: UN peacekeepers caught up in a crushing military defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a batter is out when the stumps are broken before they reach the crease, one way of being sent off.

clue.text: Studious bod rejected firm's book missing right information

indicators.note: rejected says the word is thrown back, read in reverse

parts.note: a wonk is a studious person

indicators.note: missing says the right letter is dropped from the book

parts.note: a ledger is a company's account book

explanation.surface: A swot rejects a company's account book because a page on rights is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: WONK reversed gives KNOW; LEDGER missing R gives LEDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts and learning acquired are what someone knows, their stock of facts.
